name: Beijing Municipal Health Commission
quote: 互联网诊疗医师接诊前需进行实名认证，确保由本人提供诊疗服务。其他人员、人工智能软件等不得冒用、替代医师本人提供诊疗服务。
quote_label: 关于贯彻落实《互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）》的通知, 第五条 (issued 2023-12-29; primary page read 2026-09-20)

provenance.note: EN gloss of the quote: Internet diagnosis physicians must complete real-name authentication before receiving patients, to ensure that the physician personally provides the diagnostic and treatment service. Other personnel, artificial-intelligence software and the like must not impersonate or substitute for the physician in providing diagnostic and treatment services. This is a short municipal implementing notice under the national 互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）, jointly issued by six Beijing bodies (health, cyberspace, market regulation, healthcare security, TCM, drug administration). D1=2: art. 5 requires institutions to upload to the municipal supervision platform the ID number, photograph, qualifications, place and scope of practice and years of clinical work of every physician practising online; art. 2 requires institutions to dock with the platform and accept supervision; art. 3 folds platform-docking and data reporting into the institutions licence verification, with joint health/insurance follow-up on refusal to report. Every online encounter is traceable to a named, authenticated individual. D2=2: 确保由本人提供诊疗服务 plus art. 4 - the physicians primary practice institution 应掌握医师互联网诊疗活动的开展情况并加强管理. D3=0: the notice says nothing about telling the patient anything - there is no disclosure or labeling provision at all. D4=2: the clause quoted is one of the most explicit anti-impersonation provisions in the corpus, naming 人工智能软件 directly. D5=1: there is no review-the-output requirement, because AI is not admitted to the loop to begin with; the human is not validating machine output, the human is the whole loop. Scored 1 rather than 2 to avoid double-counting the D4 ban - the document specifies no validation procedure for any AI-assisted output. D6=1: art. 3 commissions the municipal internet-diagnosis quality-control centre to build an evaluation mechanism, and art. 4 requires 3 or more years of independent clinical experience - but this is evidence about the practitioner, not evidence for the clinical claim. c2_fit=partially: the line lands in roughly the right place - the diagnostic encounter (proof scarce at the moment of delivery) is reserved absolutely, while art. 7 carves general health-information services that are not diagnosis out of the supervision regime entirely (cheaply checkable, low stakes). But the stated rationale is impersonation control and 防范化解互联网诊疗安全风险, not verification economics; the boundary is drawn on identity integrity and happens to coincide. c3=Relational: trust is anchored in the named, registered, real-name-authenticated physicians personal presence. The evidential elements present (credential verification, quality-control evaluation) are evidence about the person, not about the claim. twilight=false.
